set.fitNote: RESTATEMENT CORRECTION, 29 September (Christian). 04.a and 05.a carry the SAME basisEvidence — setup_guidance "Mark wide channels along both touchlines" — and 04.a's own fitNote already recorded "Holds only the contact in ‘runs along its touchline’ (same as 05.a)". They were two representations of one authored placement, not two competing authored values, and they collided on three channel elements by string inequality alone. The parenthetical is now a gloss beside the value rather than a second REQUIRED_RANGE contribution. Source, strictness, valueStatus and provenance are unchanged, and no engine semantics changed. "One channel on each lateral side" remains NOT held: touchline-adjacent does not say which touchline, and S2 has no side attribute (ledger).

items.why: two spellings of one authored placement were entailing two different values on S6, producing three collisions that were never a knowledge conflict. Making the parenthetical a gloss leaves one value, preserves both items and their shared source, and changes no engine semantics

set.fitNote: MARKED RELATIONAL 29 September, then TYPED AS DISTINCT_ON the same day once Christian adopted the assertion. The restatement had written one joint constraint as a per-element bound on O4, so it reached three separate object classes as three independent bounds — and three independently valid placements can still violate it. It is therefore NOT a bound on any one line, and contributes none. It is carried instead as a DISTINCT_ON assertion over the object collection: members differ pairwise on O4 and O5. No metric, no minimum separation — the source says explicitly "no separation distance" — no inferred geometry, and no line of its own. Realization chooses each placement against its own bound and is refused if the resulting SET violates it. Value, source and provenance are unchanged.

items.why: a joint constraint over a set of candidates had been flattened into a per-element bound, which both misstates the knowledge and would license a per-line realization freedom that cannot honour it. Typed as DISTINCT_ON so each placement stays freely choosable within its own bound while the set is checked jointly

set.fitNote: TYPED, 30 September, on the SD-86 precedent and exactly as the neutral count was (C29c). The channel width was AUTHORED all along — requirement RANGE, basis AUTHORED, value "across-interval width about 6-10 m", from setup_guidance "(~6-10m wide depending on field size)". Only the value STRING defeated the parser, which typed it QUALITATIVE and left it bounding nothing a check could read. On a 40 x 30 m session it fits inside the 30 m across dimension, so it yields concrete geometry here; on an envelope where it would not, the proportional question is still open and is the owner decision returned rather than guessed at.

items.why: an explicitly authored numerical range was sitting unreadable in prose, so the channel width bounded nothing a spatial check could use. Typing it changes no authored content and makes the bound checkable; the absent SCALING rule is returned separately and not invented

set.basisEvidence: Christian, 2026-10-01: "Promote GF2-14.b, equal outfield counts, from ASSUMED to owner-authored canonical knowledge." With the caution attached to it: "Please preserve the ability for other selected authoritative knowledge to establish numerical asymmetry where the learning problem requires it. Equal team numbers should not become an engine-level universal assumption."
set.fitNote: PROMOTED 1 October. It was ASSUMED, and by §3 an assumed item bounds but never entails — which is why the roster could not derive. It is now owner-authored and entails. IT REMAINS AN ITEM OF GF2, not an engine rule: a game form that authors asymmetry displaces it through the ordinary displacement mechanism (SD-90), so equality is knowledge about THIS game form and never a universal. TYPED AS A COMPARISON 3 October (Christian): "AM-16 already introduced COMPARES for comparison between represented properties, so please don't introduce another mechanism or continue relying on prose matching for 'equal'." The equality is now DECLARED structurally rather than detected by matching the word in this item's prose — that was how an AUTHORED item reading 'unequal between the teams' once licensed an equal division. The authored value, basis, status and provenance are unchanged. NOT YET EVALUABLE, and the reason is the register's own: both operands name P2, a row owned by performers.teams[], so each matches BOTH members, and comparison.stillOpen says 'No aggregate function is named (each, some, the sum, the greatest) for a comparison ranging over several matched elements. An engine refuses such a comparison rather than choosing one.' Naming the members individually is not open either, because no knowledge item may target a member's opaque handle. So the equality is readable and refused, which is reported rather than worked around.

items.why: the roster could not derive because equality bounded without entailing; promoting it closes that without making equal team numbers an engine-level assumption. Typed as a comparison on 3 October so the engine reads a declared relationship instead of matching prose, which is where the 'unequal' near-miss came from

set.fitNote: EXISTS per team becomes RANGE >=1 PER_TEAM. The clause 'not mirrored or identical in kind' is a non-claim, declared on DV1. TYPED 4 October (Christian): "Please type the explicitly authored '>=1' objective count into its proper structured field under the same SD-86 principle we've already applied. This is the same normalization class as the previous explicit cardinalities, not new knowledge." The 1 is verbatim in the authored value and countBounds could not read it: its minimum pattern wants a 'min 1' form and its bare-digit match is anchored, so '>=1' matched neither and the claim arrived with no cardinality at all. That is the same shape as NEUTRAL-01.a's '>= 1 (no authored maximum)' (C29c) and PCG-08's 'at least 2 teams' (C37), both already typed. Minimum 1, maximum null, exactly as authored; no maximum is introduced because none is authored. The prose value is unchanged so the source stays visible beside its typed form. This is the one claim the 3 October removal of the minimum-of-one substitution newly exposed: before typing, it was the only existential claim in the corpus whose cardinality was unreadable, and it is reached only through the corpus-wide run - no learning goal selects RPC-001.

items.why: an explicitly authored '>=1' was sitting unreadable in prose, so the claim carried no cardinality and, once the engine stopped substituting a minimum of one, became the single unreadable claim in the corpus. Typing it restores the number the author wrote and changes no authored content

set.fitNote: The structural shadow of 'not a technique exercise'. The rest of that clause is PCG-17. TYPED 3 October (Christian): "Please move the explicitly authored 'at least 2 teams' into the appropriate typed cardinality field under SD-86. This is normalization of authored knowledge, not inference. Preserve the meaning exactly: minimum 2, with no additional maximum unless independently authored." The number 2 is VERBATIM in the authored value and the parser could not read it: countBounds anchors a bare-digit match and finds no 'min 2' form in 'at least 2 teams (an attacking team and a defending team)', so the claim reached the engine as 'at least one, no maximum' — an authored number silently weakened. Minimum 2, maximum null, exactly as authored; no maximum is introduced, because none is authored here. The prose value is unchanged so the source stays visible beside its typed form. Typing it changes no authored content and restores the number the author wrote; it also removes the dependence of the shared-collection population on which claim happened to be readable

set.fitNote: STALE CLAIM CORRECTED, 3 October (Christian): "Please trace the four stale P2 fitNotes and correct the claim that no comparison requirement exists." This note read "the bound is read from other elements and rows, which no requirement kind holds (SCHEMA LOCAL)". That was true when written and has been obsolete since 20 September: AM-16 registered the requirement kind COMPARES for exactly this shape, and SD-23 gives it an operand form for a quantity derived from other rows. The authored value is unchanged, and so is its AUTHORED basis and REQUIRED_RANGE status. It is NOT typed as a comparison here, because two things the register leaves open would have to be chosen to do so, and neither is mine: the right-hand side 'P2(other team) - P5' is a derived quantity and no named derived rule is registered for it (operandForms requires '{ derived: <named rule>, args }'); and both sides name P2, a row owned by performers.teams[], so each matches every member, which comparison.stillOpen says an engine must refuse rather than resolve by choosing an aggregate. So the honest state is: expressible in FORM, not yet evaluable, for two named and reportable reasons rather than for the absence of a requirement kind. Counting outfield players only remains the original's reading (KNOWLEDGE).

items.why: the note declared a schema limitation that AM-16 removed on 20 September, so it misreported the reason this item cannot be checked. Correcting it names the two real blockers — an unregistered derived rule and the unnamed aggregate — without typing the item or touching its authority

set.fitNote: STALE CLAIM CORRECTED, 3 October (Christian). This note read "Equality across elements is not a value any requirement kind holds (SCHEMA LOCAL)". AM-16 registered COMPARES on 20 September and its own examples include 'count(A) = count(B)', so equality across elements IS a relationship the grammar holds — it is simply not a VALUE, which is the part the note had right: comparison.relation says NARROWS and 'It never entails a value and never entails existence'. NOT PROMOTED, on his instruction: "Where an item is only a TYPICAL_EXAMPLE or otherwise lacks authority, don't promote it merely because COMPARES now exists." The basis stays ASSUMED and the status stays PREFERRED_DEFAULT — the only evidence remains text the original itself marks TYPICAL_EXAMPLE (NEUTRAL-11) — so by SD-27 it bounds, never entails, and could not create an authoritative collision even once typed.

items.why: the note gave a schema reason that no longer exists for something that is in fact an authority limitation. Separating the two keeps the real constraint visible and avoids the item being promoted merely because the mechanism arrived

set.fitNote: STALE CLAIM CORRECTED, 3 October (Christian). This note read "A sum across rows has no requirement kind (SCHEMA LOCAL)". AM-16's second operand form is precisely a sum across rows — SD-23: 'a deterministically derived quantity whose inputs are SUPPORTED represented game properties: { derived: <named rule>, args }'. So the kind exists. What does not exist is a NAMED derived rule for this sum, and comparison.inputsMustBeSupported adds that 'A derived operand whose input the game states but nothing supports is not computable'. Naming such a rule is an authoring act, not an engine one, so it is reported rather than invented. Basis stays ASSUMED and nothing is promoted. The generalisation of '= 12' to E1 and the observation that the explicit rule exists only as engine wording (not a source) are unchanged.

items.why: the note blamed the absence of a requirement kind for what is actually the absence of a named derived rule. The distinction matters because the first is closed and the second is an open authoring decision

set.fitNote: RESTATED 2 October (Christian), ruling option (i): "WIDEZONE-08.d should not establish a third S2 region. Based on its authored meaning and its own note, its claim is that the existing Wide Zone channel population carries the perceptual-reference function/member. The COUNT 2 comes from the already-established channel population; it does not entail two additional regions or a third region. So please restate it as a property statement over the two established lateral channels, rather than an S2 existence assertion." Its own original note already said as much: "COUNT 2 (from WIDEZONE-03) so both channels carry the member (RC-16)" -- the 2 was a reference to the established population, not a second assertion of it. It therefore moves from S2 (the collection, where an existence requirement mints an element) to S4 (space.regions[].functions, where a member is asserted of whichever regions the selector reaches). NOT authorized and NOT done: making it one specific side (nothing authored establishes that perceptual-reference belongs to wide-left rather than wide-right), and identity-by-narrowing. The distinction preserved: a statement that a property applies to N existing members does not thereby assert the existence of N additional members. Form follows the only other S4 item in the corpus, which is an EQUALS naming a member ("access (forbidden as a member of functions)", strictness EXCLUSION); this is its positive counterpart, so EQUALS with strictness SUPPORTING. EQUALS is outside EXISTENCE_REQUIREMENTS and S4 is a FIELD, so it cannot mint an element by either route -- which is the point of the ruling.

items.why: it was asserting existence on the collection row while its content was a property of the channels already established; moving it to the functions row keeps element existence and properties of established elements distinct

set.fitNote: TYPED 2 October on the SD-98 precedent. The referents were the prose "both wide channels of this contract, each a referent", and SD-58 forbids comparing open text as identity, so GA-MODIFIER-OVERLAP could not evaluate the modifier at all. This item types the FIRST referent; WIDEZONE-11.c carries the second. Two items rather than one array because V8b's registered valueType is "one property per referent" and that semantics is now operational (register `multiplicity: SET`): the two are MEMBERS and accumulate, where an array value would be read as a permitted set and make the line a choice between the channels. DETERMINACY COMES FROM RULING C33: before it, "both wide channels of this contract" answered to three classes and typing it would have required selecting between them. Since C33 the contract establishes exactly two -- WIDEZONE-02.a (wide-left) and WIDEZONE-03 (wide-right) -- so "both" names them and nothing is selected between, inferred or substituted. SD-63 is untouched for ordinary open text.
